newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Maybank profit above expectations.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Maybank profit above expectations.

text.p: Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank), Malaysia's biggest banking group, said on Saturday its net profit rose 39 percent to 654.57 million ringgit ($262.8 million) for the half year ended December 31, 1996, exceeding most analysts' forecasts.
Maybank had been expected to post a net profit of about 580-600 million ringgit.
Maybank managing director Amirsham Aziz attributed the improved performance to operational efficiency, better interest margins and a higher loan volume.
"We are quite satisfied with this performance as it reflects a higher rate of profitability," he told a media briefing to announce the results.
Net profit rose 27 percent from the previous corresponding period to 469.69 million ringgit.

"For every ringgit of capital funds invested in our operations, we secured a gross return of 36.8 cents per year. Compared with the corresponding period of last year, it was an improvement of over 13 percent," Amirsham said.
Maybank said its group pretax profit was up 36 percent to 1.08 billion ringgit, against 796.34 million previously.
The bulk of the group's earnings came from Maybank, the country largest commercial bank, which posted a net profit of 438.34 million ringgit, up 35 percent.
The strongest profit growth came from Mayban Securities, the group's stockbroking arm, which reported a 148 percent increase in pretax profit to 50.2 million ringgit.
Maybank-controlled Kwong Yik Bank Bhd posted a pretax profit of 84.3 million ringgit, up 38 percent.

Kwong Yik's profit was included in the group's results as the proposed sale of Maybank's 75 percent stake in Kwong Yik to stockbroking group Rashid Hussain Bhd for 2.16 billion ringgit has not been completed.
Amirsham said he expected group results for the second half of the year to still include some of Kwong Yik's profits.
When asked if the sale of its Kwong Yik stake would affect group earnings, Amirsham said proceeds from the sale "should be able to compensate or even help improve our bottomline".
Maybank's loan growth was maintained at 17 percent, while deposit growth moderated to 17 percent from 28 percent in the previous corresponding period.
Analysts had expected slower loan growth.
Total loans for the group rose 19 percent to 63.17 billion ringgit in the first half.
Amirsham expected steady loan growth in the second half.
On competition from merged banks, Amirsham said Maybank has been preparing itself and was not worried.
"We have a very good market share. We see it as a challenge for us," he said.
Analysts have said that competition from merged banks was unlikely to affect Maybank's performance in the next few years.

Local banks have been urged to become bigger and better capitalised through mergers to face coming competition from foreign institutions when Malaysia liberalises its financial services industry by 2005 under its World Trade Organisation committments.
($1 = 2.49 ringgit)
